notes: Company background: mid-market SaaS that provides embedded product analytics and in-app assistants for B2B SaaS customers.
Primary drivers: predictable latency for in-app chat, tighter data controls for enterprise customers, cost predictability as usage scales.
Hosted API evaluation: positive — easy onboarding, Console traces were useful; however prefix caching and KV eviction behavior needs clarity for long chat sessions.
Dedicated ask: isolated GPU pool + VPC peering to satisfy enterprise customers and to hit P95 latency targets.
Procurement/legal: redlines center on indemnity cap, data processing specifics (subprocessor list), audit rights, and a 12-month data retention default — QLS wants shorter retention for transcripts.
Quote from Head of Product: 'We need guarantees on tail latency and an on-call escalation path — downtime impacts customer SLAs directly.'
POC findings: batching and pre-warm suggestions reduced median latency but tail remains ~300ms at peak; SE suggested tiny model variant fallback to reduce cost during storms.
Pricing sensitivity: QLS expects committed monthly spend with burst credits; current draft pricing for Dedicated is ~30% above internal target — in negotiation.
Security/touchpoints: they require SSO (SAML), SOC2 attestation, KMS integration for customer keys, and contract-level audit logging retention options.
Operations note: QLS will likely need managed incident reporting + extended log retention as paid add-on (requested in security call).
